Class JumpNudge

java.lang.Object
dev.swordai.core.rl.JumpNudge
public final class JumpNudge extends Object
A push towards one choice in one situation, added to what the network itself says: jump, a few ticks after it has swung, standing on the ground with the opponent on screen. A jump lasts about as long as the weapon takes to come back, so one made then has the fighter coming down as the next swing is ready, which is what a critical hit is made from.

The moment matters to the tick. A jump is on its way down from its 7th tick to its 11th, and the weapon is back 11 ticks after the swing. Taken off 3 to 5 ticks after the swing, the fighter has four or five ticks in which a swing is a critical hit; taken off with the swing or the tick after, it has one, and has landed before it can use it.

Why it is needed: a control that has only just been unlocked is used at random, and a random jump makes a fighter worse. So the first thing learned about jumping is not to, everywhere, long before a jump at the right moment has been tried often enough to be told apart. Rewards alone do not get past that.

The push is part of the policy, not a correction of its actions: it is added to the network's output before an action is drawn and again, with the strength it had on that step, when the step is learned from. So what is learned is exactly about the policy that was played, and the network still decides: it can lean against the push or with it. The strength is set from outside (see Curriculum.jumpNudge) and fades to nothing, at which point the network jumps on its own or not at all.

    • inOwnJump

      public static boolean inOwnJump(float[] vec)
      Whether the fighter is in the air by its own doing: off the ground, and not hit in the last twelve ticks (in the air after a hit is the opponent's doing).

    • inAir

      public static boolean inAir(float[] vec)
      Whether the fighter is off the ground, whoever put it there. For as long as it is, the swing is the crit model's (see ActorNet): also on the way up after the opponent's hit, where the swing has to be kept for the way down if a punish crit is to come of it.

    • critMoment

      public static boolean critMoment(float[] vec)
      Whether a critical hit can be in the making: the fighter is in a jump of its own, or it is off the ground and coming down, whoever put it there. Coming down after the opponent's hit has knocked it up is where a punish crit is made. In these ticks the sprint key is the crit model's, and W/S too unless it is busy getting out of a combo (see ActorNet).

    • critSwingReady

      public static boolean critSwingReady(float[] vec)
      Whether a swing made now, in the air, would be a critical hit as far as the fighter can tell from its own body: it is coming down, the weapon is back, and it is not sprinting. (The game asks for more than nine tenths of the charge half a tick on; eleven ticks after the last swing that is so.)

      The sprint is part of it since 0.13.0. The game makes no critical hit of a swing by a sprinting player, and a fighter knocked into the air by a hit is sprinting more often than not. The crit model lets go of the sprint on its first tick coming down; the server hears of that at the end of the tick. A swing on that same tick is a sprint hit made in the air and uses the weapon up; one tick later it is the punish crit.
